nodes.statement: Imported principles, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 3-6 pp. 9-12): a computation variable is a set S of at least two possible attributes for which all permutation tasks are possible with side-effects (Section 3 p. 9); a variable S is clonable if the cloning task R_S(x0) = union_{x in S} {(x, x0) -> (x, x)} is possible with side-effects for some preparable blank attribute x0 (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10); an information variable is a clonable computation variable, and an information medium is a substrate with at least one information variable (Section 4 p. 10). Distinguishability is defined afterward in Section 5 (eq. (4) p. 11) by mapping into an information variable, avoiding circularity, and every information variable is then shown to be distinguishable. Principle III (interoperability, Section 6 p. 12) states that the composite S1 + S2 of two substrates with information variables S1 and S2 is an information medium with information variable S1 x S2.
nodes.bottleneck: The interoperability principle (Principle III, Section 6 p. 12) constrains composite information variables to include S1 x S2 in the source's framework. It is not shown to select the Hilbert tensor product, local tomography or any positive cone, so it does not discharge FQ-GAP-TENSOR-UNIQUENESS.

nodes.statement: Finite statement to formalize over Q(i). Take the qubit with the six Pauli eigenstates as rays. (a) The attributes Z={|0>,|1>} and X={|+>,|->} are each cloneable by a completely positive trace-preserving map (copy in the basis). (b) The union of Z and X is not cloneable: the exact relation |0><0|+|1><1| = |+><+|+|-><-| holds in Herm(2), and the images under rho to rho tensor rho differ by a nonzero matrix (the Gram entry 1/2 on |00><11| and |11><00|), so no linear map clones all four. (c) A subset of the six states is cloneable if and only if any two of its members are equal or orthogonal; hence the maximal cloneable subsets are exactly the three antipodal pairs. Criterion for (c): completely positive trace-preserving maps cannot decrease fidelity, which forces the overlap squared to equal the overlap to the fourth power, so the overlap is 0 or 1; the converse is the basis copy.
nodes.bottleneck: Exact linear algebra on Gaussian rationals; statement (c) needs a Lean or Python-Fraction formulation of the fidelity argument for rays. The link to the imported definition of a superinformation medium is a reading of definitions.

The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.

nodes.statement: Finite statement to formalize. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit at each point; for a subset O of P let A(O) be the matrices on the qubits in O, acting as identity elsewhere. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 gives A(O1) inside A(O2). (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then A(O1) and A(O2) commute. (c) The spacelike relation is symmetric and irreflexive and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 0 and 1 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. Statements (a) and (b) are immediate for tensor-product nets; the target records that the repository does not yet state them and that the content of Haag-Kastler locality (commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics) is absent because this net has no dynamics.

nodes.statement: Finite statement to formalize. Let H be the n-qubit space, A a set of sites, A(A) the matrices on A, and Omega a unit vector over Q(i). Then A(A)Omega equals H if and only if the reduced state of Omega on the complement of A has full rank 2^|A^c|, if and only if Omega is separating for A(A^c). Reason: with Schmidt rank r across A and its complement, A(A)Omega equals H_A tensor the range of the complementary marginal, of dimension 2^|A| r. Exact instances: a product vector is cyclic only for A equal to all sites; the three-qubit GHZ vector is not cyclic for any single site and is cyclic for every pair of sites; the three-qubit W vector is not cyclic for any single site and is cyclic for every pair. The finite statement is a rank condition on entanglement, in contrast to the continuum property, which holds for every bounded open region.
nodes.bottleneck: Statement and instances are exact rank computations over Q(i). A Lean proof of the equivalence for general n is open. The relation to the continuum theorem is an analogy: finite dimension has no translation group or spectrum condition.

nodes.statement: Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Section 1 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. records.name: Deutsch 2013: laws as statements about possible and unachievable tasks
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1210.7439; nothing in the paper is used as a premise of any repository result.
records.summary: Deutsch (2013, arXiv:1210.7439, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4 and Section 1.2 p. 5) proposes to state physical laws as statements about which physical transformations (tasks) can be caused to happen and which cannot, in place of dynamical laws plus initial conditions, together with the composition principle (Section 1.2 p. 5), computation media (Section 2.6 eq. (9) pp. 13-14) and Einstein locality on composite substrates (Section 3.10 p. 33). This node records the proposal as published.

records.summary: Imported vocabulary, audited against Deutsch (2013, Section 1.1 eqs. (1)-(2) pp. 2-4) and Deutsch-Marletto (2015, Section 2 pp. 6-8): a task is a set of ordered input/output attribute pairs of a substrate; a constructor causes the transformation and retains its ability to do so again; a task is possible when the laws of nature impose no limit short of perfection on how accurately it can be performed and how well a constructor can retain its ability to perform it again, and not possible otherwise; Principle I (Section 2 p. 8) states that the state of a composite substrate S1 + S2 is the pair of states on S1 and S2 and a construction on S1 changes only the S1 state. records.summary: Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563) formulate a constructor theory of information by defining computation variables (Section 3 p. 9), clonable variables and information media (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10) prior to distinguishability (Section 5 eq. (4) p. 11), avoiding the circularity of Section 1 eq. (1) p. 3. Section 7 (p. 20) and Section 8 (pp. 20-24) define superinformation media and derive non-distinguishability, no-cloning of non-orthogonal states, complementarity and unpredictability from Principles I-IX. records.name: Imported: information media and the interoperability principle
records.obligation: The interoperability principle (Principle III, Section 6 p. 12) constrains composite information variables to include S1 x S2 in the source's framework. It is not shown to select the Hilbert tensor product, local tomography or any positive cone, so it does not discharge FQ-GAP-TENSOR-UNIQUENESS.
records.summary: Imported principles, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Sections 3-6 pp. 9-12): a computation variable is a set S of at least two possible attributes for which all permutation tasks are possible with side-effects (Section 3 p. 9); a variable S is clonable if the cloning task R_S(x0) = union_{x in S} {(x, x0) -> (x, x)} is possible with side-effects for some preparable blank attribute x0 (Section 4 eq. (3) p. 10); an information variable is a clonable computation variable, and an information medium is a substrate with at least one information variable (Section 4 p. 10). Distinguishability is defined afterward in Section 5 (eq. (4) p. 11) by mapping into an information variable, avoiding circularity, and every information variable is then shown to be distinguishable. Principle III (interoperability, Section 6 p. 12) states that the composite S1 + S2 of two substrates with information variables S1 and S2 is an information medium with information variable S1 x S2.

records.summary: Imported definition, audited and corrected against Deutsch and Marletto (2015, arXiv:1405.5563, Section 6 pp. 14-18 and Section 7 p. 20): an information observable is an information variable X whose attributes satisfy double-complement closure x = u_x under distinguishability (Section 6, Principle VIII p. 16); a superinformation medium is an information medium with at least two information observables X and Y that contain only mutually disjoint attributes and whose union X union Y is not an information observable (Section 7 p. 20). Sections 8.1 and 8.3 (pp. 20-22) show under Principles III, IV, VI, VII, VIII and IX that X union Y is neither distinguishable nor clonable. The repository neither adopts this definition as a primitive nor claims that its finite carriers satisfy Principles I-IX.

records.name: Finite target: cloneable and non-cloneable attributes of a qubit
records.obligation: Exact linear algebra on Gaussian rationals; statement (c) needs a Lean or Python-Fraction formulation of the fidelity argument for rays. The link to the imported definition of a superinformation medium is a reading of definitions.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize over Q(i). Take the qubit with the six Pauli eigenstates as rays. (a) The attributes Z={|0>,|1>} and X={|+>,|->} are each cloneable by a completely positive trace-preserving map (copy in the basis). (b) The union of Z and X is not cloneable: the exact relation |0><0|+|1><1| = |+><+|+|-><-| holds in Herm(2), and the images under rho to rho tensor rho differ by a nonzero matrix (the Gram entry 1/2 on |00><11| and |11><00|), so no linear map clones all four. (c) A subset of the six states is cloneable if and only if any two of its members are equal or orthogonal; hence the maximal cloneable subsets are exactly the three antipodal pairs. Criterion for (c): completely positive trace-preserving maps cannot decrease fidelity, which forces the overlap squared to equal the overlap to the fourth power, so the overlap is 0 or 1; the converse is the basis copy.

records.name: Marletto 2016: constructor theory of probability
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1507.03287 Sections 4-7; its decision-theoretic premises (T1-T2, R1-R4, A1-A2) are distinct from the frame-function hypotheses of GP-IMPORT-GLEASON.
records.summary: Marletto (2016, arXiv:1507.03287) formulates unpredictability in superinformation media via the non-existence of an X-predictor constructor (Section 4 pp. 21-22), defines X-indistinguishability equivalence classes and X-partitions of unity [f(z)_x] through the limiting ensemble fraction constructor D_x^(N) under conditions E1-E2 (Section 5 pp. 23-29), and shows that in a decision-supporting superinformation theory (conditions T1-T2 and R1-R4, Table 1 p. 32) a player automaton Gamma satisfying decision axioms A1-A2 (Section 6.2 pp. 35-36) values an X-game of chance G_X(y) by the additive expectation V{G_X(y)} = sum_{x in X} f(y)_x x (Section 7 eqs. (16), (18), (20) pp. 41-47). This node records the paper's results.

records.name: Marletto 2016: constructor theory of thermodynamics
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1608.02625 Sections 5-7; the repository has no thermodynamic substrate or adiabatic-accessibility relation.
records.summary: Marletto (2016, v5 2017, arXiv:1608.02625) defines work media as substrates with at least three equally-spaced energy attributes admitting an adjacent-pair swap on two replicas (so work variables are information variables by Principle VII, Section 5 pp. 27-31), states the First Law as interoperability of work media (Law I, eq. (4) p. 32), and defines adiabatic possibility {x -> y} as possibility with side-effects on work variables only (Section 5.3 p. 33). Section 6 (pp. 34-42) defines heat media, Principle IX (interoperability of heat media, p. 38), the Second Law (Law II, p. 39: existence of heat attributes h1, h2 with {h1 -> h2} adiabatically possible and {h2 -> h1} not adiabatically possible), an entropy function via the adiabatic 'is-like' relation (pp. 39-41), and the Zeroth Law (Law X, p. 42), deriving Kelvin's statement in Section 7 (pp. 42-44). This node records the paper's results.

records.name: Marletto-Vedral and Bose et al. 2017: gravitationally mediated entanglement witness
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:1707.06036 and arXiv:1707.06050; the repository makes no physical claim about gravity.
records.summary: Marletto and Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 1-4, Fig. 1) argue within constructor theory that if a mediator M locally couples two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 (via Q1 <-> M <-> Q2 with no direct Q1-Q2 coupling) and generates entanglement from a product state, then M must carry at least two incompatible observables (a superinformation medium), and propose testing gravitationally induced phases between two interferometric masses; Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-5, eqs. (1)-(8)) independently propose a spin-correlation entanglement witness W = |(sigma_x^(1) tensor sigma_z^(2)) + (sigma_y^(1) tensor sigma_y^(2))| > 1 (eq. (8) p. 4) for two Stern-Gerlach interferometers interacting through Newtonian gravity phases delta phi_+- and delta phi_-+ (eqs. (2)-(4) p. 2). This node records both papers; no experiment is claimed to have been performed.

records.name: Imported inference: entanglement through a mediator indicates a non-classical mediator
records.obligation: The inference (arXiv:1707.06036 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1707.06050 pp. 1-2) is an assumption of this branch. It does not use or support any repository Lean result.
records.summary: Imported inference, audited against Marletto-Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 2-3) and Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-2): if two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 start in a separable state, interact only locally through a mediating system M (Q1 <-> M and M <-> Q2, with no direct Q1-Q2 interaction, Principle I locality), and end in an entangled state of Q1 + Q2, then M cannot be a classical medium (in Marletto-Vedral, M must have at least two disjoint incompatible observables whose union is not an information variable; in Bose et al., any mediator modeled by local operations and classical communication cannot create entanglement). The repository has no gravity model; TFQ-0084 is a finite shadow only.

records.name: Finite target: a phase interaction entangles; local operations do not
records.obligation: Statements (a) to (c) are exact determinant and rank facts. Statement (d) needs the witness construction of DS-QM071 specialized to this family. No physical claim is attached.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize over Q(i). For u in Q(i) with |u|=1, the two-qubit vector psi_u = (1,1,1,u)/2 has coefficient matrix M_u = [[1,1],[1,u]]/2 of determinant (u-1)/4. (a) psi_u is a product vector if and only if u=1. (b) The squared concurrence is 4|det M_u|^2 = |u-1|^2/4; for u=(3+4i)/5 it equals 1/5. (c) For all 2x2 matrices A and B over Q(i), rank(A M B^T) <= rank(M), so local operations cannot raise the Schmidt rank of a product vector, while diag(1,1,1,u) applied to the product vector (1,1,1,1)/2 gives psi_u. (d) For u != 1 an exact separating functional on the 4x4 density matrix exists relative to the product family, in the form of DS-QM071. The physical inference from such entanglement to a non-classical mediator is imported, not part of this target.

records.name: Finite strict posets and spacelike separation in CausalOrder.lean
records.obligation: The theorem name incomparability_not_transitive_c1 overstates its statement. A genuine non-transitive example (the four-element N poset) is part of the finite net target of this stage.
records.summary: lean4/CausalOrder.lean defines FiniteStrictPoset n (an irreflexive transitive relation on Fin n) and spacelike separation (x differs from y and neither precedes the other). It establishes spacelike_symm and spacelike_irrefl; on the named examples C1 (0<1, 0<2) and C2 (the four-element diamond) it establishes c1_spacelike_1_2, c2_causal_0_3, order_independence_witness (C1 and its dual differ) and the table entries c1_mu_spacelike_vanishes and c2_mu_top_bottom (value 1). Scope: three decided examples, no general causal-set theory. The theorem named incomparability_not_transitive_c1 states only that e1 and e2 are spacelike in both orders and that e1 is not spacelike to itself; it does not exhibit a failure of transitivity of spacelike separation. The table c2_mu is checked entry by entry; the Lean file does not state the Mobius recursion for it.

records.name: Product tables are no-signalling in NoSignallingCore.lean
records.obligation: The quantum statement that commuting local measurements at spacelike separated points give setting-independent marginals is not stated in this file.
records.summary: lean4/NoSignallingCore.lean establishes, for natural-number-valued tables of the product form P x y a b = PA x a * PB y b in which each PB y sums to 1 over a listed outcome set, that the marginal on the first party does not depend on the second party's setting (product_noSignalling, marginalA_product), and that the table sig, in which the first outcome equals the second setting, has a setting-dependent marginal, so NoSignallingBA fails (sig_signals). Scope: product tables over the naturals with outcome lists; no quantum states, no commuting local observables, no relation to the posets of CausalOrder.lean.

records.name: Haag and Kastler 1964: local nets of observable algebras
records.obligation: Record only. The checkout holds no copy of the 1964 print article; the standard postulate list is checked in secondary sources (arXiv:math-ph/9903028 Section 1 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1607.03901 Section 6 pp. 28-30), while the primary 1964 numbering remains to be audited against the print text.
records.summary: Haag and Kastler (1964) formulate quantum field theory through a net that assigns to bounded spacetime regions the algebras of observables localized there, with the standard structural requirements later grouped as isotony (larger regions have larger algebras), locality (algebras of spacelike separated regions commute) and Poincare covariance, and with states as positive functionals. This node records the framework; the paper's own list of postulates is not reproduced.

records.name: Imported: a causal spacetime with a net of local algebras
records.obligation: Held outside the programme by declaration, as recorded for the light cone in the trunk node named in the gap route.
records.summary: Imported structure: a spacetime with a causal order, and a family of unital star-algebras A(O) indexed by regions O with isotony (O1 inside O2 gives A(O1) inside A(O2)) and commutation of A(O1) and A(O2) when O1 and O2 are spacelike separated. The repository has finite strict posets (lean4/CausalOrder.lean) and finite matrix algebras, but no net over regions of a continuum and no Minkowski light cone; DS-QM033-064-074-083-QHELD-CONTINUUM records the light-cone causality as an external L2 lift.

records.name: Finite target: isotony and locality for a net on a finite poset
records.obligation: The net is kinematical. Dynamics, a time-slice property and covariance are not modelled, so the statement is the finite shadow of two axioms and nothing more.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. For a FiniteStrictPoset P on n points put one qubit at each point; for a subset O of P let A(O) be the matrices on the qubits in O, acting as identity elsewhere. (a) Isotony: O1 inside O2 gives A(O1) inside A(O2). (b) Locality: if every point of O1 is spacelike to every point of O2, then A(O1) and A(O2) commute. (c) The spacelike relation is symmetric and irreflexive and not transitive: on the four-element N poset 0<2, 1<2, 1<3, points 0 and 1 are spacelike, 0 and 3 are spacelike, and 1<3 are related. Statements (a) and (b) are immediate for tensor-product nets; the target records that the repository does not yet state them and that the content of Haag-Kastler locality (commutation forced by causal separation of dynamics) is absent because this net has no dynamics.

records.name: Reeh and Schlieder 1961: cyclicity of the vacuum
records.obligation: Record only. The precise hypotheses (spectrum condition, vacuum uniqueness, covariance) are to be audited against the paper.
records.summary: Reeh and Schlieder (1961) study the unitary equivalence of Lorentz-invariant fields and obtain what is cited as the Reeh-Schlieder property: for a positive-energy, Poincare covariant theory with a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for the algebra of any bounded open region. The paper is in German and the checkout holds no copy; the statement and hypotheses are recorded from citations.

records.name: Imported: Reeh-Schlieder property and its continuum hypotheses
records.obligation: The inputs of the property are the continuum Hilbert lift and the Stone theorem, which the repository records as open. The gap route below lists them.
records.summary: Imported property: in a net of local algebras on Minkowski space with a translation action whose generators have positive spectrum (spectrum condition) and a vacuum vector, the vacuum is cyclic for every local algebra, and under further hypotheses separating for the algebra of a region with spacelike complement. The proof uses analytic continuation of translations, hence a continuous translation group and its generator (Stone's theorem) on an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Both are open nodes of the repository.

records.name: Finite target: cyclicity of a state for a subsystem algebra is a rank condition
records.obligation: Statement and instances are exact rank computations over Q(i). A Lean proof of the equivalence for general n is open. The relation to the continuum theorem is an analogy: finite dimension has no translation group or spectrum condition.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. Let H be the n-qubit space, A a set of sites, A(A) the matrices on A, and Omega a unit vector over Q(i). Then A(A)Omega equals H if and only if the reduced state of Omega on the complement of A has full rank 2^|A^c|, if and only if Omega is separating for A(A^c). Reason: with Schmidt rank r across A and its complement, A(A)Omega equals H_A tensor the range of the complementary marginal, of dimension 2^|A| r. Exact instances: a product vector is cyclic only for A equal to all sites; the three-qubit GHZ vector is not cyclic for any single site and is cyclic for every pair of sites; the three-qubit W vector is not cyclic for any single site and is cyclic for every pair. The finite statement is a rank condition on entanglement, in contrast to the continuum property, which holds for every bounded open region.

records.name: Epstein and Glaser 1973: the role of locality in perturbation theory
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the Numdam full text (AIHPA_1973__19_3_211_0); nothing in the paper is used as a premise of a repository theorem.
records.summary: Epstein and Glaser (1973, Ann. Inst. H. Poincare A 19, 211-295, Abstract p. 211, Section 1.1 pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223, and Section 5 pp. 231-237) give an inductive construction of the perturbation series S(g) = 1 + sum_{n>=1} (i^n / n!) int T_n(x_1,...,x_n) g(x_1)...g(x_n) dx in which each order T_n is constructed from lower orders by causal factorization outside the total diagonal and by splitting causal distributions with scaling degree bounds on the diagonal. This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Imported: causal factorization of the scattering matrix
records.obligation: Audited against Epstein-Glaser (1973) eqs. (9), (30) and Brunetti-Fredenhagen (2000) eq. (2) and Condition P3. The continuum distribution extension has no counterpart in the repository's finite posets.
records.summary: Imported property, audited and corrected against Epstein and Glaser (1973, Section 1.1 condition (C.A.) pp. 214-215, Section 2.1 condition (Caus. 1) eq. (9) p. 218, Section 2.2 eq. (30) p. 223) and Brunetti and Fredenhagen (2000, arXiv:math-ph/9903028, Section 1 eq. (2) p. 4 and Section 3 Condition P3 p. 15): the scattering operator satisfies V(g, h1+h2) = S(g)^{-1} S(g+h1+h2) = V(g, h1) V(g, h2) (and at g=0, S(g1+g2) = S(g1) S(g2)) whenever supp h1 does not intersect the causal past of supp h2, written supp h1 cap (supp h2 + V^-) = empty (which includes spacelike separation as well as causal future separation, not only supp h1 inside the causal future of supp h2). Equivalently at each order n, the time-ordered operator-valued distributions factorize as T(P union Q) = T(P) T(Q) whenever {x_i : i in P} cap ({x_j : j in Q} + V^-) = empty (eq. (30) p. 223; Condition P3 p. 15), and renormalization reduces to extending time-ordered products across the total diagonal. The repository has neither operator-valued distributions nor a continuum Minkowski causal cone.

records.name: Finite target: time-ordered products over linear extensions of a poset
records.obligation: The elementary swap lemma needs a Lean proof for general n. The relation to Epstein-Glaser is an analogy.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. For a FiniteStrictPoset P and matrices A_x (x in P) on a common finite space, the ordered product along a linear extension (a listing of P in which x<y puts x before y) is the same for every linear extension whenever A_x and A_y commute for all spacelike pairs x,y, because any two linear extensions differ by swaps of adjacent spacelike elements. Exact checks: all linear extensions of the diamond C2 (two of them) and of the N poset, with Pauli matrices; and the sign flip when two spacelike elements carry anticommuting Pauli matrices. This is the finite counterpart of causal factorization. The distribution extension and the ultraviolet content of the Epstein-Glaser construction have no finite counterpart.

records.name: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin 1987: space-time as a causal set
records.obligation: Record only. Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 3 p. 6) and Reid (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section II p. 2) were audited in full; the 1987 PRL print article is not held in the checkout.
records.summary: Bombelli, Lee, Meyer and Sorkin (1987) propose that spacetime at the smallest scales is a discrete structure, a causal set: a locally finite set with a partial order encoding past and future. They examine how a Lorentzian manifold can approximate such a set, note that effective dimensionality can vary with length scale, and sketch a quantum dynamics. Sorkin's Valdivia notes (2003) are a later survey. This node records the proposal.

records.name: A finite causal set is a FiniteStrictPoset
records.obligation: Definitional only. Nothing about manifold-likeness, dimension or the continuum limit is asserted.
records.summary: Reading of definitions. A causal set in the sense of the source is a locally finite partially ordered set; in the strict-order form its relation is irreflexive and transitive, and local finiteness is automatic on a finite set. This is the structure FiniteStrictPoset n of lean4/CausalOrder.lean. The Python class CausalSet in code/python/src/general_relativity/causal_set.py builds a poset from relations, takes the transitive closure and refuses cycles. The identification involves no sprinkling, no embedding in a Lorentzian manifold and no dynamics.

records.name: Finite target: ordering fraction, Myrheim-Meyer dimension and Hasse diagrams as exact rationals
records.obligation: Everything is rational arithmetic on named finite posets. The dimension estimator is a heuristic for sprinklings; the finite estimate on a small poset carries no manifold statement.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. The ordering fraction of a finite causal set is the exact rational r = 2R/(n(n-1)), with R the number of strictly related pairs (CausalSet.ordering_fraction). In Sorkin (2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0309009 Section 7 p. 16), the expected ordering fraction of a Poisson sprinkling into a d-dimensional Minkowski causal interval normalized by binom(N,2) is f(d) = (3/2) Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2 + 1) / Gamma(3d/2 + 1) = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (2 Gamma(3d/2)) (in Reid 2003, arXiv:gr-qc/0207103 Section III eq. (5) p. 5, normalizing by <N>^2 instead of binom(N,2) gives f(d)/2 = Gamma(d+1) Gamma(d/2) / (4 Gamma(3d/2))), with exact rational values f(1)=1, f(2)=1/2, f(3)=8/35 and f(4)=1/10 recomputed in Python with fractions.Fraction; the Myrheim-Meyer estimator inverts f. Targets: (i) the n x n grid with the componentwise product order has r = (n+3)/(2(n+1)) (recomputed in Python with fractions.Fraction: n=2 gives 5/6, matching the diamond C2 of CausalOrder.lean with 5 related pairs out of 6, n=3 gives 3/4, n=4 gives 7/10, n=5 gives 2/3, n=6 gives 9/14, n=7 gives 5/8, and the limit 1/2 equals f(2); this is an observation about a lattice, not an instance of the sprinkling theorem). (ii) An exact rational dimension decision: for a rational r in (0,1], which of d=1,2,3,4 has f(d) nearest, with ties reported. (iii) The Hasse diagram (covering relation) is the unique transitive reduction; its link count and the Mobius values of C1 and C2 agree with the table entries of CausalOrder.lean.

records.name: Maldacena 1997: large N superconformal field theories and supergravity
records.obligation: Record only. The duality is a conjecture supported by checks in the source literature.
records.summary: Maldacena (1997, arXiv:hep-th/9711200, Section 2 eqs. (2.1)-(2.5) pp. 3-5, conjecture p. 9) takes the low-energy decoupling limit of N parallel D3-branes (eq. (2.1)) and conjectures that four-dimensional U(N) N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory is dual to type IIB string theory on AdS_5 x S^5 with radius R^2 / alpha' = sqrt(4 pi g_YM^2 N) (eq. (2.5)) and N units of five-form flux, alongside M2/M5-brane and AdS_3 counterparts in Sections 3-5. This node records the conjecture as published.

records.name: Gubser-Klebanov-Polyakov and Witten 1998: the correlator dictionary
records.obligation: Record only. The dictionary is not reproduced.
records.summary: Gubser, Klebanov and Polyakov (1998, arXiv:hep-th/9802109, Section 2 eq. (2.5) p. 4 and Section 3 eq. (3.14) p. 8) and Witten (1998, arXiv:hep-th/9802150, Section 2.3 eq. (2.11) p. 11 and Section 2.5 eqs. (2.32)-(2.33) p. 17) formulate the AdS/CFT prescription identifying the CFT generating functional of boundary operators O coupled to boundary sources phi_0 with the bulk partition function <exp int phi_0 O>_CFT = Z_string(phi_0) (approximated at large N by exp(-I_sugra(phi)) on AdS_{d+1}), with conformal dimension Delta(Delta - d) = (m R)^2, Delta = (d + sqrt(d^2 + 4(m R)^2))/2 for a scalar of mass m. This node records the two papers.

records.name: Imported: bulk gravity and boundary conformal field theory are equivalent
records.obligation: The continuum inputs are not constructed: FQ-GAP-CONTINUUM-HILBERT-LIFT and the finite-to-continuum interface TFQ-0085 are open.
records.summary: Imported as an assumption, not as a result of this repository: a quantum gravity theory on an asymptotically anti-de Sitter spacetime has the same observables as a conformal field theory on its boundary. The duality is a conjecture. It presupposes continuum quantum field theory (a Hilbert space, unitary evolution, operator algebras) and a continuum gravity theory; the repository records both as open or held outside the programme.

records.name: Ryu and Takayanagi 2006: holographic entanglement entropy
records.obligation: Record only.
records.summary: Ryu and Takayanagi (2006, arXiv:hep-th/0603001, Section 1 eq. (1.5) p. 2) propose that the entanglement entropy S_A of a spatial subregion A in a (d+1)-dimensional CFT dual to static AdS_{d+2} is given by S_A = Area(gamma_A) / (4 G_N^(d+2)), where gamma_A is the static minimal bulk d-surface anchored on partial A, and check in Section 2 (eqs. (2.1), (2.5)-(2.6) p. 3) that in AdS_3/CFT_2 the geodesic length reproduces S_A = (c/3) log((L/(pi a)) sin(pi l / L)) under the Brown-Henneaux relation c = 3R / (2 G_N^(3)). This node records the proposal as published.

records.name: Imported: entropy of a boundary region equals minimal surface area over 4G
records.obligation: No source supplies a dictionary from the repository's finite areas to the surface areas of the formula.
records.summary: Imported formula, as the source states it at leading order in Newton's constant: S(A) = Area(minimal surface anchored on the boundary of A) / (4 G). It presupposes the von Neumann entropy of a boundary reduced state on a continuum Hilbert space and the area of a surface in a bulk geometry. The repository has an exact von Neumann entropy dichotomy for algebraic spectra and an exact rational Regge area proxy that is not the Einstein-Hilbert action; neither is a minimal-surface area in a bulk geometry.

records.name: Almheiri, Dong and Harlow 2015: bulk locality and quantum error correction
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the full text of arXiv:1411.7041 on 2026-10-22; the finite 5-qubit reconstruction instance is the separate target ADS-LOGICAL-RECONSTRUCTION-TARGET.
records.summary: Almheiri, Dong and Harlow (2015, arXiv:1411.7041) resolve the radial-commutativity puzzle of bulk local operators by formulating the low-energy bulk Hilbert space as a code subspace H_code inside the boundary CFT Hilbert space: a bulk operator phi(x) in the causal wedge (or entanglement wedge, Section 3.4) of a boundary subregion A can be reconstructed as an operator O_A supported on A that acts identically to phi(x) on H_code (Section 3.1 eq. (3.3) p. 11, equivalent to [O, E_a P E_b^dagger] = 0 on the erasure errors of A^c in Section 3.2 eqs. (3.10), (3.15) pp. 13-15, illustrated by the three-qutrit code in Section 2.2 eq. (2.4) p. 8). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Harlow 2016: the Ryu-Takayanagi formula from quantum error correction
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against the full text of arXiv:1607.03901 (Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 5.1) on 2026-10-22; the theorem is not formalized in this repository.
records.summary: Harlow (2016, arXiv:1607.03901, Theorem 1.1 pp. 3-4 and Section 5 Theorem 5.1 pp. 20-26) establishes in finite-dimensional operator-algebra quantum error correction that for a code subspace H_code in H_A tensor H_{A-bar} and a von Neumann algebra M on H_code with commutant M' and center Z_M = M cap M', three conditions are equivalent: (i) complementary recovery of M on A and M' on A-bar, (ii) existence of a positive central area operator L_A in Z_M such that for every code state rho-tilde, S(rho-tilde_A) = Tr(rho-tilde L_A) + S(rho-tilde, M) and S(rho-tilde_{A-bar}) = Tr(rho-tilde L_A) + S(rho-tilde, M'), and (iii) conservation of relative entropy S(rho-tilde_A | sigma-tilde_A) = S(rho-tilde | sigma-tilde, M). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Pastawski, Yoshida, Harlow and Preskill 2015: holographic quantum error-correcting codes
records.obligation: Record only. The abstract itself calls the codes toy models.
records.summary: Pastawski, Yoshida, Harlow and Preskill (2015, arXiv:1503.06237) define a 2n-leg perfect tensor (Section 2 Def. 2 p. 5: proportional to an isometric tensor for every bipartition into k <= n inputs and 2n - k outputs), construct the 6-qubit perfect stabilizer tensor from the [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme et al. (1996, arXiv:quant-ph/9602019 Table I; HaPPY Appendix A.1 eqs. (A1)-(A7) pp. 24-25), and place it on the {5,4} hyperbolic pentagon tiling to obtain an isometric bulk-to-boundary code (Section 3 Thm. 1 p. 7) in which connected boundary regions of holographic states satisfy S_A = |gamma_A| log v (Section 4.1 Thm. 2 p. 8) and general regions satisfy the greedy-geodesic lower bound (Section 4.2 Thm. 3 eq. (4.10) p. 10). This node records the paper as published.

records.name: Finite target: the five-qubit code gives a six-leg perfect tensor
records.obligation: GF(2) symplectic arithmetic over a 64-element group. The repository has stabilizer-code checks for other codes but not this one.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. The [[5,1,3]] code of Laflamme, Miquel, Paz and Zurek has stabilizer generators XZZXI, IXZZX, XIXZZ, ZXIXZ and logical operators XXXXX and ZZZZZ. Its Choi state is the six-qubit stabilizer state with generators g tensor I (four of them), XXXXX tensor X and ZZZZZ tensor Z. Claim: this state is a perfect tensor, that is, every bipartition with at most three legs on one side has a maximally mixed marginal, equivalently every non-identity element of its 64-element stabilizer group has weight at least 4. Expected weight distribution: 1 element of weight 0, 45 of weight 4, 18 of weight 6 (the hexacode six-qubit state); all twenty 3|3 bipartitions have entropy 3 bits; the minimum weight of a nontrivial logical operator is 3.

records.name: Finite target: boundary entropies of a six-tensor patch against minimal cuts
records.obligation: Exact GF(2) linear algebra on a 26-qubit stabilizer state. The bond-count cut is graph min-cut. The correspondence to a surface area is the imported formula and is not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. Contract six copies of the perfect tensor of the previous target on the {5,4} pentagon tiling: one central tensor and its five edge-neighbours. The edge-neighbours are not adjacent to each other, so the patch has 20 dangling boundary legs (4 per outer tensor) and 6 bulk legs. Fix every bulk leg in the logical zero state. For every contiguous interval A of boundary legs, compute the entropy S(A) in bits by GF(2) rank and compare it with the minimal number of bonds cut by a curve separating A from its complement, listing the intervals with equality. The source states that the Ryu-Takayanagi formula holds exactly in many cases (regions whose minimal cut is a greedy geodesic), not for every region; the target is to determine which intervals satisfy it on this patch.

records.name: Finite target: logical operators of the five-qubit code live on any three qubits
records.obligation: Exact GF(2) check over the normalizer (64 elements). The identification with bulk reconstruction is the picture of the source and is not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. For the [[5,1,3]] code, each of the ten triples T of physical qubits supports a representative of each nontrivial logical class (the classes of XXXXX, ZZZZZ and their product), and no pair of qubits supports any nontrivial logical operator. Equivalent statement: erasure of any two qubits is correctable. This is the smallest exact instance of the subregion-reconstruction picture of bulk operators.

records.name: Gap: repository Regge areas versus the area term of the minimal-surface formula

records.obligation: Record only. Both normalization conventions (l_P^2 vs 8 pi gamma l_P^2, per Ashtekar-Lewandowski Section 3.3 footnote 6 p. 16) and the general vertex-puncture formula (eq. (4.9) p. 18) were audited against the papers on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Rovelli and Smolin (1995, arXiv:gr-qc/9411005, Section 1 eqs. (1)-(2) p. 4 and Section 4 eqs. (47)-(48) p. 28) and Ashtekar and Lewandowski (1997, arXiv:gr-qc/9602046, Section 3.3 eq. (3.20) p. 16 and Section 4.1 eqs. (4.7)-(4.9), (4.12) pp. 18-19) compute discrete spectra for loop-quantum-gravity area (and volume) operators. In the convention {A_a^i(x), E_j^b(y)} = G delta_a^b delta_j^i delta^3(x,y) used in both papers, the general area eigenvalue is (l_P^2 / 2) sum_v sqrt(2 j_v^(d)(j_v^(d)+1) + 2 j_v^(u)(j_v^(u)+1) - j_v^(d+u)(j_v^(d+u)+1)) (eq. (4.9) of gr-qc/9602046), which for simple transverse punctures without tangential edges (j^(d)=j^(u)=j_i, j^(d+u)=0) equals l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)) = (l_P^2 / 2) sum_i sqrt(p_i(p_i+2)) with p_i = 2 j_i (eq. (2) and eq. (47) of gr-qc/9411005; eq. (4.12) of gr-qc/9602046); as Ashtekar and Lewandowski note in Section 3.3 footnote 6 (p. 16) and Engle et al. write in arXiv:0711.0146 Section V eq. (36) (p. 11), restoring the 8 pi G gamma factor from the gravitational action and Barbero-Immirzi parameter gamma multiplies this spectrum by 8 pi gamma, giving 8 pi gamma l_P^2 sum_i sqrt(j_i(j_i+1)). (The nonzero trivalent volume formula in eq. (1) and eq. (37) of gr-qc/9411005 was corrected in the erratum Nucl. Phys. B 456 (1995) 753, where trivalent vertices have zero volume.) This node records both papers and their normalization conventions.

records.name: Finite target: exact area levels as sums of square roots
records.obligation: Exact arithmetic in Q(sqrt 2, sqrt 3, sqrt 5, sqrt 6, sqrt 7, ...). The physical constant, the Immirzi parameter and the gauge-invariance constraint on admissible puncture lists are not part of the target.
records.summary: Finite statement to formalize. With the dimensionless area a = sum over punctures of sqrt(j(j+1)) for spins j in {1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, ..., 3}, each term is an exact algebraic number: sqrt(3)/2, sqrt(2), sqrt(15)/2, sqrt(6), sqrt(35)/2, sqrt(12)=2 sqrt(3) for j=1/2, 1, 3/2, 2, 5/2, 3. Square roots of distinct squarefree positive integers are linearly independent over Q, so two multisets of punctures have equal area if and only if the sums agree after reducing each root to squarefree form. Targets: (i) the table of exact levels for at most four punctures with j<=3; (ii) the degeneracies, which arise from non-squarefree radicands and from the equality criterion, for example one puncture of spin 3 has the same area as four punctures of spin 1/2 (2 sqrt(3) = 4 x sqrt(3)/2); (iii) the smallest nonzero level is sqrt(3)/2.

records.name: Ponzano and Regge 1968: semiclassical limit of Racah coefficients
records.obligation: Record only. The 1968 chapter has no arXiv record and is not held in the checkout; its asymptotic formula is verified in Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 p. 22 and Section 6.1 p. 61).
records.summary: Ponzano and Regge (1968) give the leading asymptotic form of the 6j symbol (Racah coefficient) for large spins, with separate forms for the classically allowed and forbidden regions, and introduce a state sum for three-dimensional gravity whose phase matches the Regge action of a tetrahedron. The formula was reached by conjecture and numerical checks. This node records the chapter by title and publication details.

records.name: Roberts 1999: classical 6j symbols and the tetrahedron
records.obligation: Record only. Audited against arXiv:math-ph/9812013 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61 on 2026-10-22.
records.summary: Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Section 1 Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61) establishes by geometric quantization of the 8-sphere and stationary phase on the symplectic reduction that for an admissible 6-tuple of integers a, b, c, d, e, f (where a = 2j labels the (a+1)-dimensional irreducible representation of SU(2)) whose side lengths form a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron tau of positive volume V(tau) > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the rescaled 6j symbol {ka, kb, kc; kd, ke, kf} has the k -> infinity asymptotic expansion sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(tau) k^3)) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (k a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) + O(k^{-5/2}). Since a tetrahedron of side lengths j_r = a_r/2 has volume V_j = V(tau)/8, substituting 2 / (3 pi V(tau)) = 1 / (12 pi V_j) and (a_r + 1)/2 = j_r + 1/2 recovers the Ponzano-Regge prefactor (12 pi V_j)^{-1/2}. This node records the paper's theorem.

records.name: Imported: Ponzano-Regge asymptotics of the 6j symbol
records.obligation: The asymptotic statement is a limit of real-valued quantities; the repository's exact finite targets do not establish a limit.
records.summary: Imported asymptotic form, audited against Roberts (1999, arXiv:math-ph/9812013, Theorem 1 eq. (2) p. 22 and Section 6.1 eqs. (12)-(13) p. 61): for large spins with edge lengths l_r = j_r + 1/2 = (a_r + 1)/2 (where a_r = 2 j_r), when the six lengths bound a non-degenerate Euclidean tetrahedron of positive volume V > 0 and exterior dihedral angles theta_r, the 6j symbol behaves asymptotically as (12 pi V)^{-1/2} cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (j_r + 1/2) theta_r + pi/4) (equivalently sqrt(2 / (3 pi V(a))) cos(sum_{r=1}^6 (a_r + 1) theta_r / 2 + pi/4) where V(a) = 8 V is the volume for side lengths a_r = 2 j_r), and decays exponentially when the Cayley-Menger squared volume is negative (Lorentzian tetrahedron, Section 6.2 p. 62). The phase is the Regge action of the tetrahedron.

Tuples with V^2 > 0 lie in the allowed region (a Euclidean tetrahedron exists) where the imported asymptotics predict oscillation; tuples with V^2 < 0 lie in the forbidden region where it predicts decay.
